sources.constraint_header:
/*
Package flate compresses and decompresses DEFLATE and zlib streams.

The whole stream is passed in at once and the output is appended to dst, so
neither direction needs an io.Reader or an io.Writer. A limit above zero bounds
the decompressed output; whatever was decoded is returned even when the error is
not nil.

	out, err := flate.DecompressZlib(nil, src, 0)

	d := flate.NewDecompressor()
	out, err = d.DecompressZlib(out[:0], src, limit)

Compression takes a level from 1 to 9, or zero for the default, matching the
levels compress/flate uses.

	out, err := flate.CompressZlib(nil, src, 0)

	c := flate.NewCompressor()
	out, err = c.CompressZlib(out[:0], src, 9)

A Compressor and a Decompressor hold the tables their calls reuse, so a caller
doing many of either should keep one rather than call the package functions. A
single one of them is not safe for concurrent use; the package functions are,
because they take one from a pool.
*/
package flate

/*
Package pngn decodes and encodes PNG images.

	img, err := pngn.Decode(r)

[Decode] returns *[image.Gray], *[image.Gray16], *[image.NRGBA],
*[image.NRGBA64], *[image.Paletted], *[image.RGBA] or *[image.RGBA64], the same
type image/png returns for the same input. The package registers itself with
[image.RegisterFormat].

Every color type and bit depth the specification defines is read, with or
without Adam7 interlacing, and tRNS is applied. A malformed file gives
[ErrInvalid] and a well formed one this package cannot decode gives
[ErrUnsupported].

	img, err := pngn.Decode(r, &pngn.Options{PixelLimit: 1 << 24})

[DecodeConfig] reports the dimensions and color model as the header stores
them.

# Encoding

	err := pngn.Encode(w, img)

[Encode] chooses the color type and bit depth from the image, the same way
image/png does, so a decode and a re-encode keeps a file's shape.
[EncodeOptions] selects the compression level, the row filter, and Adam7
interlacing, which image/png cannot write.

	err := pngn.Encode(w, img, &pngn.EncodeOptions{
		CompressionLevel: pngn.BestCompression,
		Interlace:        true,
	})

# Metadata

[Metadata] holds every ancillary chunk: text, EXIF, an ICC profile, the color
space and HDR chunks, physical size, time, and the chunks this package does not
interpret. [DecodeMetadata] reads them without decoding pixels, and
[EncodeOptions.Metadata] writes them, so a decode and re-encode keeps what
image/png throws away.

	meta, err := pngn.DecodeMetadata(r)

	err := pngn.Encode(w, img, &pngn.EncodeOptions{
		Metadata: &pngn.Metadata{
			Text: []pngn.Text{{Keyword: "Software", Value: "pngn"}},
		},
	})

[DecodeExif] parses the eXIf chunk and [Options.AutoRotate] applies the
orientation it carries.

# Damaged files

[Options.Partial] returns the rows a truncated file did carry rather than an
error, which is what a viewer wants from a download that stopped.
[Options.IgnoreCRC] decodes a chunk whose checksum is wrong. Neither is on by
default, and nothing this package decodes panics on any input.

# Animation

	anim, err := pngn.DecodeAll(r)

[DecodeAll] returns every frame of an APNG, composited onto the canvas and the
size of it, with the delay of each in seconds and the loop count. A file with no
acTL chunk comes back as one frame. [EncodeAll] writes one, using the first
frame as the default image so that a decoder which does not know APNG still sees
something, and writing each later frame as only the rectangle it changes.
*/
package pngn
